noiseSdAtSkill0.why: Perception noise on option scores (scores are fractions of the best achievable outcome, 0..1) for a decision maker with no skill: options within ~20% of each other look alike.

noiseSdAtSkill1.why: Noise for a top specialist: they usually land within 3–5% of the best option, i.e. the 90–97% of achievable result that plan 5.19 asks for.

blunderChanceAtConsistency0.why: How often an erratic decision maker badly misjudges one option. Weak staff lose by spread, not by average (plan 5.19).

blunderChanceAtConsistency1.why: Even the steadiest person misreads a situation about once in two hundred decisions.

blunderSize.why: Size of a blunder, in score units: large enough to promote a clearly bad option over the best one.

rapportNoiseReduction.why: Share of perception noise removed at full rapport with the player: a long-standing working relationship halves the gap to what the player would have picked (plan 5.19).
